Add The New York Post on Google Originally Published by: Illinois mother charged with murder in death of 2-year-old ICE officer pleads not guilty to lying about Minneapolis shooting involving Venezuelan man Lindsay Clancy mistrial declared after jury deadlocks in killings of her three children For decades, the prevailing story of the Manson murders held that Charles Manson masterminded a murderous plot to ignite a race war inspired by the Beatles. But Joe Berlinger argues the infamous story never added up. The true crime filmmaker directed a three-part Netflix docuseries titled “Conversations with a Killer: The Charles Manson Tapes .” It features previously unreleased prison audio from the cult leader and some of his “Manson Family” members. In 1969, the career criminal who surrounded himself with runaways and other lost souls directed his followers to commit a series of murders in and around Los Angeles. Prosecutors argued the killings were part of Manson’s “Helter Skelter” plan to ignite a race war. But after studying the previously unreleased recordings, Berlinger argues the murders were instead a desperate attempt to cover up “a series of blunders. “This whole idea of starting a race war was a false idea,” Berlinger told Fox News Digital. “He certainly believed a race war was coming, or at least that’s what he told his followers to control them. But the murders, in particular the Tate and LaBianca murders , were an attempt to get associate Bobby Beausoleil out of prison. He told his followers, ‘He’s my friend. You guys owe me a favor. Let’s get him out of prison.’ 8 American actress Sharon Tate in London. T Getty Images “The truth is I believe, and others believe, that if they had succeeded in this crazy idea of getting Bobby Beausoleil out of prison, I think Manson would’ve killed him because he was a liability,” said Berlinger. “But listening to those tapes made the story come alive, not these crazy conspiracy theories and myths that turned Charles Manson into the most mythologized figure in the history of true crime. Berlinger traces the chain of events that led to the murders to a botched drug deal. According to the documentary , Manson invited members of the Straight Satans motorcycle club to Spahn Ranch to protect him from the Black Panthers, whom he feared, offering them access to his female followers in exchange 8 Accused murderer Charles Miller Manson, 34, is led to and from a courthouse in Inyo County, California. Mirrorpix via Getty Images “[Follower] Tex Watson tried to steal money from a drug dealer named Bernard ‘Lotsapoppa’ Crowe, who wants his money back,” Berlinger explained. “Manson goes out there and doesn’t intend to kill him, but thinks he killed him, a Black Panther.” According to the documentary, Watson stole Crowe’s money, prompting Crowe to threaten retaliation. Manson later shot Crowe and mistakenly believed he had killed him. Crowe was not a Black Panther “He goes back to Spahn Ranch and becomes paranoid that the Black Panthers are going to come after him. He becomes friends with Bobby, tells him to join the family and also to help protect the ranch. Bobby becomes tight with some bikers who were also invited to protect the ranch from the Black Panthers. 8 Charles Manson in “Conversations with a Killer: The Charles Manson Tapes,” which aired on Aug. 12, 2026. ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection But the motorcycle gang wanted more than just women. The documentary says Beausoleil brought them drugs he obtained from music teacher Gary Hinman. The bikers were unhappy with the quality of the supply, and Beausoleil was pressured to recover their money “Bobby tries to get his money back from Gary and can’t get it,” said Berlinger. According to court records, during the confrontation, Manson arrived at Hinman’s home and slashed Hinman’s face with a sword, cutting him from his left ear toward his chin. Over the course of about three days, Manson’s followers tortured Hinman. Beausoleil later stabbed Hinman to death and wrote the words “Political Piggy” on a wall in Hinman’s blood, along with an animal paw print intended to implicate the Black Panthers 8 Manson family members and murder suspects Susan Atkins, Patricia Krenwinkle and Leslie van Houton. Bettmann Archive “Gary Hinman is killed because Manson comes in, wields a sword and then tells Bobby ‘finish the job’ to cover the tracks,” Berlinger said. Beausoleil was arrested about a week after Hinman’s body was discovered. Berlinger said Beausoleil was driving Hinman’s vehicle and had “the murder weapon stupidly in the stolen car.” Berlinger said Manson wanted police to believe Hinman’s murder was the work of the Black Panthers to cast suspicion away from Beausoleil. He noted the attempt to free Beausoleil became the catalyst for the murders that followed 8 A mugshot of Charles “Tex” Watson. Watson was convicted of murder for his part in the killings of Sharon Tate and others while a member of the “Manson Family.” Bettmann Archive On Aug. 9, 1969, Manson’s followers murdered five people at a Los Angeles home previously rented by music producer Terry Melcher: actress Sharon Tate, who was 8 1/2 months pregnant; coffee heiress Abigail Folger; celebrity hairstylist Jay Sebring; Polish writer Wojciech Frykowski; and Steven Parent, who had been visiting the estate’s caretaker Melcher had previously declined to sign Manson to a recording contract. “The murder is tried to be made to look like it was part of Gary Hinman’s murder,” said Berlinger. “But when Manson picks up the paper the next day, and there’s no information about these two murders being linked, they do another murder. The logic is, ‘We’ve got to make people think that Bobby, who is sitting in prison, is not guilty.’ “This was all a series of blunders, a bunch of bad, spontaneous decision-making.” 8 Actress Sharon Tate and hair dresser Jay Sebring pose for a portrait on a plane circa 1966. Michael Ochs Archives The next night, wealthy grocer Leno LaBianca and his wife, Rosemary LaBianca, were stabbed and killed in their home across town. The killers scrawled phrases including “Pigs” and the misspelled words “Healter Skelter” in blood at the crime scene. Manson was arrested in October 1969. Prosecutors maintained at trial that Manson ordered his followers to kill some of Los Angeles’ rich and famous to trigger a race war, a plan prosecutors said grew in part from his interpretation of the Beatles’ song “Helter Skelter. Manson frequently spoke about an impending race war and interpreted songs on the Beatles’ “White Album” as messages about the coming conflict, according to testimony from his followers. What remains disputed is whether those beliefs motivated the Tate-LaBianca murders or whether, as Berlinger argues, prosecutors elevated them into the central theory of their case 8 Robert ‘Bobby’ Beausoleil poses for a mugshot after being arrested for the murder of Gary Hinman at the request of Charles Manson on August 7, 1969. Getty Images “[Prosecutor Vincent Bugliosi] had to come up with a legal theory to convict a guy who actually didn’t do the killings,” Berlinger said. “Manson wasn’t even there when the Tate-LaBianca killings took place. So how do you convict somebody who wasn’t there? Well, you come up with this organizing principle that he convinced his followers that a race war was coming, and he was trying to make that race war happen. It was a brilliant legal theory, but it’s a false story.” “The Manson murders are much more tragic, but much more banal than this idea of some crazy cult trying to start a race war,” Berlinger continued. “This was a drug deal gone bad, trying to cover up Gary Hinman’s killing by doing another murder the next day to make it look like a copycat murder, which were the Tate murders. And when that murder didn’t hit newspapers like a Black Panther murder, they did the LaBianca murders. It’s a series of blunders by people who were trying to cover their tracks, not this grand scheme of ‘Helter Skelter.'” Bugliosi worked with writer Curt Gentry on a book about the case. Published in 1974, “Helter Skelter” became the bestselling true crime book of all time 8 Charles Manson, 34, arrives in handcuffs at the Inyo County Courthouse for a preliminary hearing on charges of arson and receiving stolen goods. Bettmann Archive Manson and three followers — Susan Atkins, Patricia Krenwinkel and Leslie Van Houten — were found guilty and later sentenced to death. Charles “Tex” Watson was tried separately and convicted later. Their death sentences were reduced to life in prison after the California Supreme Court invalidated the state’s death penalty in 1972 Atkins died in prison in 2009. Van Houten was released on parole in 2023. Krenwinkel and Watson remain in prison Manson died at a California hospital in 2017 while serving a life sentence. He was 83. Berlinger maintained Manson’s reputation as an evil mastermind was fueled more by myth than reality. “He wasn’t killing or ordering people to kill to get some kind of satisfaction,” Berlinger said. “He was covering up a series of blunders and just getting deeper and deeper into a hole. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c893.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor OrbÃ¡n and Serbian President Aleksandar VuÄiÄ shared more than a taste for Balkan pastries By Nick Thorpe Reporting from Belgrade Published 2 hours ago When they met in northern Serbia last November, Serbian President Aleksandar VuÄiÄ and Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor OrbÃ¡n could hardly have guessed they would both be out of power within a year. Both were ousted by popular movements - OrbÃ¡n fell first, in April, defeated by PÃ©ter Magyar's Tisza party. Then last Sunday a student movement less than two years old won Serbia's parliamentary elections by a landslide. The Tisza party in Hungary and the Student List in Serbia look very different - Tisza is centred on the personality and energy of its leader, while the students in Serbia insist they have no leadership. But the huge turnout - 79% in Hungary and 69% in Serbia, was driven by tech-savvy young people in both countries. They used AI tools to crunch numbers, identify threats to the vote, and mobilise tens of thousands of election monitors to prevent intimidation and electoral fraud by the governing parties. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Opposition activists from Hungary shared election monitoring techniques that contributed to the result in Serbia Mobilisation of voters, and the role of election monitors, played a big role in the opposition victory in both countries. Last weekend, the DE civic action group in Hungary sent 70 election monitors to Serbia, to work with students' movement representatives, visiting polling stations in the northern Serbian province of Vojvodina. During the summer, even before the election was called, they held workshops to share their experience and methods from the Hungarian election with the Serbian students. A key technique was to identify "infected" polling districts in advance - places where the surprisingly high number of votes for the governing party at previous elections suggested that voter intimidation or "chain voting" techniques were used. "From around 16:00 on election day, we noticed groups of masked hooligans - VuÄiÄ supporters - gathering near voting stations," PÃ©ter Klemm, a student activist from Subotica, told the BBC. "So we sent mobile teams, and started filming everything." Combined with the "stationary" monitors already in place, 20 to 30 volunteers at each threatened polling station acted as a strong deterrent, he believes, and prevented intimidation or fraud. OrbÃ¡n in Hungary, VuÄiÄ in Serbia, both looked invincible. Both were powerful leaders, in office for 16 and 14 years, who had taken over state institutions and established business empires overlapping the two countries. Orban chose cheese, VuÄiÄ meat, when they sat down to a quick lunch of traditional burek pastries at a small, popular town centre bakery in Subotica almost a year ago. They continued to a local winery, to talk about oil and other business deals - the planned Hungarian purchase of Serbia's Nis oil refinery. The two nationalist leaders found much in common, in business and politics, not least their friendship with Vladimir Putin in Russia and Chinese President Xi Jinping, and their strong support for Milorad Dodik, the separatist leader of the Bosnian Serbs. A high-speed railway between Belgrade and Budapest is being built with Chinese finance and know-how. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Serbian President Aleksandar VuÄiÄ and his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, made simultaneous visits to China in 2025 The parallels between the fall from power of the two men are extraordinary. Aleksandar VuÄiÄ admitted defeat at exactly 21:30 on Sunday evening, just as Viktor OrbÃ¡n did on 12 April. Few observers expected either leader to concede peacefully. There has been speculation this week that VuÄiÄ spoke to OrbÃ¡n twice on Sunday night to ask his advice - once before he conceded, and again at 23:15. And that OrbÃ¡n convinced his Serbian ally not to use force. VuÄiÄ denies that he spoke to OrbÃ¡n before he made his announcement, but acknowledges the later conversation. Viktor OrbÃ¡n, contacted by the BBC, declined to comment. An hour before polls closed in Serbia, masked and hooded vigilantes took up position in central Belgrade. During voting, similar groups were photographed at many polling stations, and blocked by election monitors. There is another strange numerical similarity. The Student List will have 140 seats in the 250-seat Serbian parliament, the same number PÃ©ter Magyar's Tisza party won in the 199-seat Hungarian parliament. Magyar was the only European leader to ring the students directly to congratulate them that evening - and probably the only one who had their number. "It is always good to hear that the story of Tisza could provide an inspiration for other nations," the Hungarian prime minister told the BBC. "The result of the Hungarian election clearly showed us that what we are doing here is right," the head of the Student List, Ilija SrdanoviÄ, said on the eve of the vote. SrdanoviÄ was one of those PÃ©ter Magyar spoke to that Sunday evening. Image source, Reuters Image caption, There has been speculation that Victor OrbÃ¡n persuaded Aleksandar VuÄiÄ not to use force, during a telephone call on election day OrbÃ¡n, 63, and VuÄiÄ, 56, may now both face prosecution for corruption and abuse of power. The judicial machinery in both countries is similar. Serbia's special prosecution service for organised crime, JTOK, and Hungary's brand new special prosecutors, known as NVVH, have similar powers. They could prove useful to each other. Hungarian companies close to OrbÃ¡n were also involved in the Novi Sad railway station construction project. The collapse of the station's canopy on 1 November 2024 - blamed on corruption, as well as negligence - killed 16 people, and acted as the catalyst for the Serbian student movement. "There was a perception in Europe that the longer the OrbÃ¡n and VuÄiÄ regimes stayed in office, the stronger they got," Ãron Timar, founder of the DE civic action group in Hungary told the BBC. "In fact they got weaker. And once society found its voice and rose up, there was no way of stopping it."
